items.title: Section: Eight Remedies, Countless Distinctions — Wholesomeness's Own Many Faces

items.zh: 當知此中，隨其所應依所說事。或於現法、或於後法，隨為一種貪、瞋、惡見，於心相續先成穢染；既被染已，由彼對治，令於是處不復相應。問：何等名為善法差別？答：或有一種，乃至十種。如本地分已廣宣說。又諸善法，或有對治雜染故，或有雜染靜息故，或有攝受可愛果故，或有相續清淨故，或有供養靈廟故，或有攝受有情故。
items.en: One should know that, corresponding to each of these bases, whenever craving, aversion, or wrong view first defiles the mind's continuity, in this life or the next, that same basis serves as its remedy, so that the mind no longer remains associated with it there. Question: what are the distinctions among wholesome phenomena? Answer: anywhere from one to ten kinds. Further, some wholesome phenomena counter defilement, some calm defilement once arisen, some secure a desirable result, some purify one's continuity, some support venerating a shrine, and some embrace sentient beings.

items.zh: 如是等類善法差別，應當了知。

items.title: Section: Seventeen Blessings of Genuine Goodness — And Why a Leaning Utility Pole Falls the Way It Always Leaned

items.zh: 復次，善法無有過失，有何功德？善法功德，有無量種。謂能淨治心，令離煩惱纏及隨眠；令於所緣無有顛倒；能令善根堅固不退；令等流行相續而轉。不為自害、不為他害、不為俱害；不生現法罪、不生後法罪、不生現法後法罪；能令受彼所生喜樂；能盡生為上首所有眾苦；又能增長涅槃勝解，能親近彼。能令財位無有退失；處眾勇猛，無懼無畏；廣大名稱。流布十方；為眾聖賢之所稱讚；臨命終時，不生憂悔；身壞已後，生諸善趣；於諸善法，令無退失；能速隨證自所求義。如是等類諸善功德無邊無量，當盡了知。
items.en: Furthermore, wholesomeness carries no fault — what benefit does it possess? Wholesomeness's benefits are countless: it purifies the mind, freeing it from affliction's grip and its latent seed... at the moment of death it generates no anxiety or regret; once the body has ended, it leads to fortunate rebirth; it prevents every wholesome quality from regressing; and it swiftly brings about whatever goal is sought. Benefits of this kind, boundless and countless, should be fully known.

items.title: Section: Fifteen Remedies, From Simple Aversion to Complete Severance — Wholesomeness's Ninth and Final Angle

items.zh: 云何建立諸善對治？由十五種。謂厭患對治故，斷對治故，持對治故，遠分對治故，所欲趣纏對治故，非所欲趣纏對治故，隨眠對治故，軟品煩惱對治故，中品煩惱對治故，上品煩惱對治故，散亂對治故，諫悔對治故，羸劣對治故，制伏對治故，離繫對治故。
items.en: How is wholesome remedy established? Through fifteen kinds: remedy through aversion, remedy through severance, remedy through sustaining, remedy through distancing, remedy towards attachment to a desired destiny, remedy towards the entanglements leading to an undesired destiny, remedy towards the latent seed, remedy towards soft-, medium-, and superior-grade affliction, remedy through settling, remedy through admonition and confession, remedy through weakening, remedy through suppression, and remedy through complete severance.

items.title: Section: Root Afflictions and Their Six Grounds — Where Craving, Aversion, and Pride Actually Take Hold

items.zh: 復次，諸染污法二相所顯。一、本煩惱，二、隨煩惱。今當先說本煩惱，後當分別隨煩惱。問：本煩惱有幾種依處？答：六。一、與無明俱，可意雜染境界；二、與無明俱，不可意雜染境界；三、與不如理作意俱，雜染境界；四、與無明俱，劣等勝有情、各別五取蘊、得未得顛倒、功德顛倒；五、與無明不如理作意俱，聽聞不正法；六、與無明不如理作意俱，於聽正法而生懈怠。
items.en: Furthermore, every defiling phenomenon manifests through two aspects: root affliction and secondary affliction. Question: how many grounds give rise to root affliction? Answer: six. First, ignorance together with a pleasing defiled object. Second, ignorance together with a displeasing defiled object. Third, improper attention together with a defiled object. Fourth, ignorance together with comparison against inferior, equal, or superior beings, one's own aggregates, confused attainment, and confused merit. Fifth, ignorance and improper attention together with hearing false teaching. Sixth, ignorance and improper attention together with laziness while hearing true teaching.

items.zh: 當知最初，欣樂和合依處；第二，欣樂別離依處；第三，於境顛倒依處；第四，陵蔑上慢依處；第五，邪執法行依處；第六，不修正行、不為還滅依處。

items.title: Section: Six Root Afflictions Defined — And Why Ignorance Accompanies Every Single One

items.zh: 問：煩惱自性有幾種？答：有六種。一、貪，二、瞋，三、無明，四、慢，五、見，六、疑。問：何煩惱與何煩惱相應？答：無明與一切。
items.en: Question: how many kinds constitute affliction's own essential nature? Answer: six — craving, aversion, ignorance, pride, view, and doubt. Question: which affliction is associated with which other affliction? Answer: ignorance is associated with all of them.

items.title: Section: Doubt Stands Alone, Craving and Aversion Never Meet, But Pride and Wrong View Travel Together

items.zh: 疑都無所有。貪瞋互相無，此或與慢見。謂染愛時，或高舉、或推求。如染愛，憎恚亦爾。慢之與見，或更相應。謂高舉時，復邪推搆。
items.en: Doubt is associated with none. Craving and aversion mutually exclude one another, though either may combine with pride or view. When defiled attachment arises, it may accompany inflated self-regard or distorted reasoning. As with attachment, so too with aversion. Pride and view tend especially to reinforce one another, since inflated self-regard often accompanies distorted, speculative reasoning as well.

items.title: Section: Wrong View Is Just Tainted Wisdom — And Why the Coarsest Affliction Is Actually the Weakest

items.zh: 問：是諸煩惱，幾世俗有？幾實物有？答：見世俗有，是慧分故。餘實物有，別有心所性。問：是諸煩惱，云何建立軟中上品？答：最後所斷名軟品，中間所斷名中品，最初所斷名上品。復由六因，諸煩惱成上品。一、婬欲所生煩惱，性多上品。二、串習所生煩惱，性多上品。三、安足處煩惱，謂根熟者，性多上品。四、不可治煩惱，謂無涅槃法者，性多上品。五、非處加行煩惱，謂於尊重福田等所，性多上品。六、有業煩惱，謂正發業者，性多上品。
items.en: Question: how many afflictions exist conventionally, and how many as genuinely distinct realities? Answer: view exists conventionally, being a portion of discernment; the rest exist as genuinely distinct mental factors. Question: how are the afflictions established as soft, medium, or superior grade? Answer: what is severed last is called soft grade; what is severed midway is called medium; what is severed first is called superior grade. Six further causes make an affliction superior: arising from sexual desire, arising from habituation, having a secure footing, that is, arising once the faculties are mature, belonging to one without potential for liberation, wrongly directed at a venerable object, and accompanied by action, that is, actively generating action.

items.zh: 問：煩惱生時，由幾煩惱事而得生耶？

blocks.text: From the good to the afflictions. The treatise lists six root afflictions and shows how they combine.
Master Cháng Bǎi: each benefit is the reverse of an affliction's fault; the faults being countless, so are the benefits. Doing good now weakens past evil karma, leaving it no chance to ripen.

Master Cháng Bǎi: on the path of preparation, hearing, reflection, and cultivation recognise suffering and its origin and give rise to weariness; that is remedy by aversion. Merely suppressing manifest afflictions is remedy by suppression.

Master Cháng Bǎi: with ignorance of impermanence and selflessness, meeting a lovely object is the ground of craving. (Untranslated, 0603a17: the six grounds are for delighting in union, delighting in separation, misperceiving objects, contempt and arrogance, wrong views of the Dharma, and not practising rightly.)
Ignorance accompanies all; doubt joins none; craving and aversion never meet, though either may join pride or view; pride and view may join.

Master Cháng Bǎi: view is set up on the mental factor wisdom; its nature is defiled wisdom. Afflictions are graded by the order of severance. Master Cháng Bǎi: what is cut first is most obvious, called "superior"; what is cut last is subtlest, called "soft". Mature adults have strong mental force, so their afflictions are fiercer.
Notice the reversal: the "strongest" affliction is the coarsest and is cut first. The subtle ones, hardly noticed, are the last to go.

quiz.q: Why are the benefits of the wholesome countless? How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate them to affliction?
options: each benefit is the reverse of a fault of affliction; those faults being countless, so are the benefits
benefits have nothing to do with affliction, the wholesome having countless benefits of itself, with no need for comparison
there are really only seventeen, "countless" being exaggeration
the benefits appear only after death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each benefit named here is the reverse of a fault of affliction; the faults being countless, the benefits are too. And doing good now reduces the force of past evil karma, leaving it no occasion to manifest. So benefit is described by contrast, which prepares the later list of affliction's faults.

quiz.q: The English has "remedy towards aversion to an undesired destiny" for 非所欲趣纏對治. Is the sense right?
options: it is reversed: the Sub-commentary says it counters afflictions binding one to undesirable destinies, not aversion to them
right: a practitioner's dislike of evil destinies is an affliction to be remedied, exactly as the treatise means, so the English stands
reversed: it should be countering craving for desirable destinies
the treatise has no such remedy, which the English adds
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary says the first counters afflictions binding one to desirable destinies, and the second counters afflictions binding one to undesirable ones. The English "aversion to an undesired destiny" reads 非所欲 as if the remedy were aimed at disliking evil destinies, which would make such dislike the thing to be cured. That is not the meaning.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish remedy through aversion and remedy through severance?
options: severing at the unobstructed path is remedy through aversion; weariness on the path of application is remedy through severance
on the path of application, weariness born of knowing suffering and origin; on the supramundane path, actually severing afflictions at the unobstructed path
the first is hating someone and the second cutting off contact, both worldly relations unrelated to the path
the two are the same under two names
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: on the path of application, hearing, reflection, and cultivation recognise suffering and origin and give rise to weariness; this is remedy through aversion. On the supramundane path, actual severing at the unobstructed path is remedy through severance. The English word "aversion" also renders 瞋, an affliction, though here it means wholesome weariness.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate grades of affliction to remedies, and what of suppression and complete severance?
options: the higher the grade the subtler, needing the highest path; suppression ends seeds, and severance subdues manifest ones
the higher the grade the coarser, so a lower path suffices; suppression subdues manifest ones, while complete severance ends seeds forever
grades have no relation to remedies, one path severing all at once, the treatise's distinction being a device
only afflictions of a scattered mind need remedy
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the higher the grade of affliction, the coarser its aspect, and a lower power of the path can counter it; merely subduing manifest afflictions is remedy through suppression, and the last, remedy through complete severance, cuts off the seeds of affliction forever. The contrast repeats that between suppression and destruction seen in earlier fascicles.

quiz.q: Among the six grounds, which afflictions arise from the first, third, and sixth?
options: a pleasing object with ignorance, aversion; improper attention with a defiled object, pride; laziness in hearing true teaching, view
a pleasing object with ignorance, pride; improper attention with a defiled object, craving; laziness in hearing, aversion, since the lazy dislike the teaching
all six give rise only to ignorance, since it is everywhere
a pleasing object with ignorance, craving; improper attention with a defiled object, ignorance; laziness in hearing true teaching, doubt
quiz.why: The treatise lists six grounds without naming their afflictions; the lecture matches them. Master Cháng Bǎi: with ignorance of impermanence and selflessness, meeting a lovely object is the first ground, of craving; improper attention towards a defiled object is the third, of ignorance; failing to understand and growing lazy in hearing true teaching is the sixth, of doubt.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say of association among the afflictions?
options: craving and aversion always arise together; ignorance does not join doubt; pride and view exclude each other, each standing apart
the six never join one another, one thought having only one
all six are always present together
ignorance joins all; doubt none; craving and aversion exclude each other but may join pride or view; pride and view may join
quiz.why: The treatise says ignorance is associated with all; doubt with none; craving and aversion mutually exclude one another, though either may join pride or view; and pride and view may also join. Master Cháng Bǎi: craving and aversion are opposed in nature and cannot arise together; wherever there is affliction there is ignorance.

quiz.q: The English has "a variant of wisdom" for 慧分. What is the problem?
options: 慧 is only good, wrong view could never belong to it, so treatise and English err, and it should be "ignorance"
分 should be "part," "variant" being an addition
見 should be "sight," unrelated to 慧
慧 extends to all moral qualities, and wrong view is defiled 慧; "wisdom" sounds praiseworthy, so "discernment" would be better
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the affliction of view is also called evil view; it is provisionally set on the mental factor 慧, so its nature is defiled 慧; joined with good, it establishes right view, and joined with evil it is evil view. As a neutral term for a factor, 慧 is poorly served by "wisdom," and the English title's "Wrong View Is Just Tainted Wisdom" shows the strain.

quiz.q: How are soft, medium, and superior grades of affliction established?
options: what is severed first is soft; midway medium; last superior
by the weight of the deed, killing superior, stealing medium, lying soft, unrelated to the order of severance
by realm: desire superior, form medium, formless soft
what is severed last is soft; what is severed midway medium; what is severed first superior
quiz.why: The treatise grades afflictions by the order of severance. Master Cháng Bǎi: what is severed last is subtlest and is called soft; what is severed first is most obvious and is called superior. So "superior" here means coarse and easily severed, not strong in the sense of hard to remove.

quiz.q: By what six causes do afflictions become superior?
options: those severed by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, the path, cultivation, and beyond learning, arranged by stage of severance
craving, aversion, ignorance, pride, view, doubt
born of sexual desire, of habituation; at a settled ground; incurable; wrongly directed; and generating karma
born of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind
quiz.why: The treatise gives six causes. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: mature adults have strong mental force, so their afflictions are fiercer and of superior grade; on the sixth: afflictions shown in bodily and verbal action are plainly visible and mostly superior. The English "arising once the faculties are mature" leaves 安足處 untranslated.
